subject: Production latency & 5xx spike — eu-west-1 (NeonBridge)
messages:
From: John Hart <john.hart@neonbridge.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Karen Liu <karen.liu@neonbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Production latency & 5xx spike — eu-west-1

Neha —

We're seeing a sudden spike in p50/p95 latency and 5xx on our production traffic served out of eu-west-1 beginning ~07:50 UTC. Traffic volume hasn't changed on our side; our observability shows a jump in 5xx from ~0.2% to ~6.8% and p50 from ~120ms to ~1.2s. This is impacting our checkout flow for a subset of customers.

Attached a small error/snippet and a short list of example request IDs (error-snippet.txt). We need a quick remediation plan and a short customer-facing status update — we're getting inbound from our ops and we promised an update within 30 mins.

Please loop in anyone who can help with routing/fallback — this looks regional.

Thanks,
John Hart
Head of Platform 
NeonBridge

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: John Hart <john.hart@neonbridge.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production latency & 5xx spike — eu-west-1

John — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We see the same symptoms on our end from 07:50 UTC. I'm escalating to SRE (Rishi) and your AM (Marissa) is looped in for comms/approval.

Immediate plan (30/60/120):
- 0–30m: triage to identify whether this is model-serving capacity, a kernel regression, or networking at the edge. Rishi will start graphs and checks.
- 30–60m: if the region remains degraded, propose a controlled geo-fallback to eu-central-1 for affected routes only (read/write routing policy change at edge).
- 60–120m: if fallback is required, execute playbook and notify you with a concise status update and remediation timeline.

Can you confirm you approve a temporary fallback to eu-central-1 if we recommend it? Also share any SLAs or constraints we should be aware of for session affinity or data locality.

I'll open an incident tracker now: https://app.redwood.com/incidents/INC-20270511-1023

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:36:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production latency & 5xx spike — eu-west-1

Quick technical summary of what I'm seeing from the serving plane logs and metrics (first 20m):
- p50 increased from ~120ms -> ~1.2s, p95 ~ 3.8s.
- 5xx rate jumped from 0.2% -> 6.8% (most 502/503).
- Token throughput dropped ~18% for eu-west-1; CPU/GPU utilization on the pool is not saturated, but request queue depth skyrocketed for the multi-tenant slice serving NeonBridge.
- KV cache hit rate dropped ~40% at ~07:49 UTC (possible cache eviction/invalidations).
- No infra-level network errors from hypervisor side; at first glance it's a workload-localized stall — likely KV cache pressure + an accidental routing of larger seq-length traffic through a slower kernel path.

Immediate suggestions:
1) Short-term: perform selective route weight shift at the edge for NeonBridge routes from eu-west-1 -> eu-central-1 (failover only for write/generation endpoints). This is reversible and preserves sessions for endpoints that are not affected.
2) If we cannot shift at edge quickly, temporarily lower model size for eu-west-1 traffic (downgrade to a smaller compatible variant) to reduce per-request latency while we diagnose.
3) Post-fallback: collect head-of-line traces and KV cache metrics; run KV re-warm.

Operational notes: the edge weight shift is an action that changes customer routing and has cost implications and potential transient session mismatches — needs customer approval. I attached the runbook we would execute if authorized (reroute-playbook.pdf).

If authorized, I can execute the route weight change now; it takes ~8–12 minutes to propagate and we should see error rate collapse within a single token window if this is purely locality.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: John Hart <john.hart@neonbridge.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:42:00 +0000
Subject: Status update: investigating production latency in eu-west-1

John —

Thanks for flagging this. Quick customer-facing status: our team has identified a regional degradation in eu-west-1 affecting generation endpoints. We're investigating root cause; our SRE recommends a temporary routing shift to eu-central-1 for affected routes to restore availability while we continue the investigation.

We will not change data retention or persist customer data in a different region; this is a routing change to a compatible serving cluster. If you approve, we will:
- Execute a targeted routing weight change for generation endpoints (8–12m propagation)
- Monitor error rates and p50/p95 during and after the change
- Provide a follow-up postmortem within 72 hours and a proposal for credits if SLAs are impacted

Please reply with a line to approve ("Approve fallback to eu-central-1") if you'd like us to proceed. We can also do a short cross-team call right now.

—Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: John Hart <john.hart@neonbridge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:47:30 +0000
Subject: Re: Status update: investigating production latency in eu-west-1

Marissa —

Approve fallback to eu-central-1. Please proceed and confirm when complete. We need a short audit entry for change management; attaching signed approval for record (signed-approval.pdf). Also please flag any expected customer-visible session impacts — we'll notify our ops channel.

—John

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: John Hart <john.hart@neonbridge.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 13:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production latency & 5xx spike — eu-west-1 (NeonBridge)

John —

Routing shift executed at 12:23 UTC; weight change targeted to generation endpoints only for NeonBridge routes. Summary of outcome:
- Propagation window: 12:23–12:35 UTC (changes verified at edge).
- Error rate: 5xx collapsed from 6.8% -> 0.4% within two minutes post-propagation.
- Latency: p50 improved from ~1.2s -> ~160ms within 10 minutes. p95 improved to ~420ms.
- Next steps: we will keep the weights shifted for the next 3 hours while we re-warm KV caches and run a targeted trace run to find root causes. Postmortem will include timeline, root cause, and a plan to avoid recurrence.

We logged the change in the incident tracker and attached timeline graphs (timeout-graphs.png). We will scope a credits proposal if SLAs were materially impacted and include that in the postmortem.

If you'd like a short exec sync, I can schedule a 30-min call with our head of SRE and your platform lead — propose 15:30 UTC today.

Thanks for the quick approval and for sending the signed doc — helped speed our audit.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
